title: a non-home box cannot drive the ticket machine — hold is not open across the LAN
intention: A client whose bus home is another box reaches a device there without asking for hold, which the LAN door refuses. The ask goes over call, and the home bus's mail wake (no_receiver) wakes the device at its home. A local reach is unchanged.
why: Measured 2026-11-12: on akienasus, with CAIRN_BUS_HOME=akiendelllinux.local:7419, `sail.py chart 1029d5146152` raised "RuntimeError: bus process: 'hold' is not open across the LAN — one of ('call', 'stats', 'verbs')". reach() goes through _wire, which always calls bus.hold, so no box but the home can drive the ticket machine.
traces_to: Law 6 (another box's bus is that box's: the far side asks, the home wakes) and ticket 5183005fa134's LAN door, kept as narrow as it was.
how: _wire holds only when the home is on this box (remote_address() is None). Red-first proof replaces remote.exchange with a recorder, so nothing dials.

clauses.claim: with a remote home, reach('codemother') sends only ops in LAN_OPS and no hold
with a home on this box, reach('codemother') sends one hold naming codemother, as before
a request through a far reach is sent as one op 'call', method 'request'

decisions.text: D1: _wire calls bus.hold(*devices) only when devices is non-empty and remote_address() is None; the docstring names why (mail wakes the device at its home; hold is not a LAN op).
D2: a red-first proof, one tooth per clause, with remote.exchange replaced by a recorder and CAIRN_BUS_HOME set per tooth; LAN_OPS restated, not imported (RULE 1).

out: cairn/devices/cairn/machines/bus (the LAN door stays as it is)
